Maria: Quick dump — after landing the compact epilogue + bias+rot fusion change on main I'm seeing a clear perf regression on short-seq workloads (seq <= 64). p99 token latency +~8%. attaching profiler summary in a sec.

Dan: Yikes. Any obvious kernel fallback happening in the logs?

Maria: Yeah, the chooser picks `flash_fuse_small_seq_v2` initially but a lot of calls then fall back to the generic epilogue kernel due to alignment/stride checks. Snippet from chooser log: 
```
choose_kernel(seq=32, bs=8) -> candidate=flash_fuse_small_seq_v2
validate: qkv_stride % 64 != 0 -> fallback to matmul_epilogue_generic
```

Sanjay: That stride validation got added with the packing changes in PR #4123 IIRC. Might be overly strict for some paged-KV layouts.

Lex: Confirmed — the new compact packing squeezes QKV tightly which changes the stride when bias+rot fusion is applied. The validation thinks memory will be misaligned.

Kevin: Perf counters also show uptick in L2 miss ratio and slowdowns from extra generic-path matmuls.

Maria: Full flame graph uploaded to the trace viewer (internal link). perf-bot: run r-202603 contains the traces.

perf-bot: r-202603 completed — baseline vs main comparison posted.

Lex: Two immediate mitigation ideas: 1) do a small memcpy prepack step that aligns the qkv buffer before calling the fast kernel (pay copy cost but avoid heavy generic matmul), or 2) relax the stride check in kernel_chooser with a conservative fallback threshold.

Dan: Copying may be cheaper for the problematic shape range (small seq, small batch) vs invoking generic kernel. We should microbenchmark the memcpy tradeoff.

Sanjay: Propose experiment matrix: 
- Exp A: memcpy prepack for seq<=64 & bs<=16 before kernel dispatch
- Exp B: chooser threshold tweak: prefer fast kernel when expected token-work < X
- Exp C: special-case paged-KV path to avoid packing that breaks alignment when page_count>1

Maria: I'll run Exp A on a dedicated bench host tonight. Command to reproduce locally: `bench_attn --model=gpt2 --seq=32 --bs=8 --runs=100 --trace` (this reliably shows the regression).

ci-bot: scheduled job `runtime-compact-epilogue-sweep` (exp A) on bench-14 for tonight.

Kevin: Also double-check KV cache interactions — paged-kv scatter can insert padding that the packing code doesn't account for, triggering the validation failure. If we prepack we need to do it upstream of paged-kv scatter to avoid extra copies.

Lex: Good call. I can sketch a minimal prepack routine that aligns to 64B and does an in-place compact+pad for small batches. If paged-kv present, we either bypass prepack or do a single contiguous copy.

Dan: I'll prototype a chooser heuristic that estimates copy_cost vs generic_cost and selects memcpy+fast-kernel when copy_cost < (generic_cost - small_margin). Keep it opt-in behind a runtime flag.

Sanjay: Timeline: Maria runs Exp A and posts numbers; Lex prototypes memcpy prepack; Dan wires chooser heuristic as a flagged opt-in; if results look good we'll merge a safe fix (copy path + flag) and follow up with smarter chooser. Aim for EOD tomorrow for canary.

Maria: Sounds good. I'll post the bench outputs here once CI finishes. Current rough numbers: baseline p99=42ms, main p99=45ms, with generic fallback p99=49ms.

Kevin: Note: set canary alert if p99 regression >10%. perf-bot: please post delta table after runs. :eyes:

perf-bot: will post delta table automatically when job completes.

Maria: Thanks all — I'll update this thread with the run IDs and flame graphs. :party:
